NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a **duty-cycle-modulated electrochemical reset** that periodically applies a short-duration anodic potential sweep to the working electrode during periods of low glucose activity, which disrupts protein adhesion and tissue encapsulation without requiring recalibration. Standard practice applies a constant potential or current at a fixed operating point; our mitigation departs by introducing a timed, high-frequency electrochemical reset that leverages existing sensor hardware and power to periodically disrupt the encapsulation process. The closest existing practice is the application of anti-fouling coatings (e.g., PEG or zwitterionic polymers), which differ by relying on passive chemical resistance rather than active electrochemical disruption of the encapsulation driving force. The intervention attacks the failure’s driving physics (protein adsorption and tissue integration) by locally oxidizing adsorbed proteins and disrupting the electrochemical double layer at the electrode-tissue interface.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the **Langmuir adsorption kinetics** for protein adhesion, modified by electrochemical desorption:  
\[ \theta = \theta_0 e^{-k \cdot \Delta E \cdot t} \]  
where \(\theta\) is the fractional surface coverage, \(\theta_0\) is the initial coverage, \(k\) is the desorption rate constant, \(\Delta E\) is the applied anodic potential, and \(t\) is the duration. A 0.5 V anodic sweep for 10 ms every 30 minutes reduces \(\theta\) by ~80% per cycle (assuming \(k = 0.1 \, \text{V}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\)), preventing the accumulation that causes signal drift. This magnitude is sufficient to maintain MARD <10% by keeping the electrode-tissue interface "fresh" without damaging tissue.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —  
| **Component/Change** | **Tag** | **Installation/Operation** |  
|----------------------|---------|----------------------------|  
| (a) Existing microcontroller firmware | (a) | Modify firmware to schedule a 10 ms anodic sweep (0.5 V vs. Ag/AgCl) every 30 minutes during low-glucose periods (glucose < 70 mg/dL) |  
| (a) Existing working electrode material | (a) | No hardware change; the reset uses the existing Pt/Ir electrode |  
| (a) Existing reference electrode | (a) | No hardware change; the sweep is referenced to Ag/AgCl |  
| (b) Commercially available voltage-boost converter (if needed for 0.5 V) | (b) | Integrate between existing battery and electrode driver (e.g., Texas Instruments TPS61200) |  
| (c) Duty cycle parameter: 10 ms every 30 minutes | (c) | Set in firmware; no new hardware |  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —  
| **Burden Category** | **Standard Practice** | **Intervention** | **Parity** |  
|---------------------|----------------------|------------------|------------|  
| Installation | None (firmware-only) | Firmware modification (a) | Same |  
| Commissioning | None | Parameter tuning (c) | Same |  
| Operation | Continuous monitoring | Continuous monitoring + periodic reset | Same (reset uses existing power) |  
| Maintenance | None | None (no new wearables) | Same |  
| Cost | None | Voltage converter (b) if needed | Same class (standard catalog) |  
**Conclusion**: Same-or-lower burden class; no new tooling or exotic parts required.

EXECUTABLE TEST —  
**Protocol**: Implant sensors subcutaneously in diabetic animal models (n=10), with 5 controls (constant potential) and 5 intervention (duty-cycle reset). Measure glucose every 6 hours for 14 days using a reference blood draw.  
**Instruments**: Commercial glucometer (reference), sensor data logger, multimeter (to verify reset voltage).  
**Pass/Fail Threshold**: Mean absolute relative difference (MARD) <10% over 14 days; if any sensor exceeds 15% MARD at any point, the test fails.  
**Duration**: 14 days.  
**Kill Criterion**: If >2 sensors in the intervention group fail MARD, the mechanism is falsified.
